findings.summary: The production publish topology does not enforce coherent-set org-first ordering: each of the three concurrent package workflows can push its package to nuget.org immediately after only its own GitHub Packages push.
evidence: Verification: docs/reports/2026-08-14-090508-coordination-churn-redesign-roadmap.md requires one orchestrator with monotonic steps and the parent M3 brief requires org-first publication for the complete coherent set.

Verification: .github/workflows/release-saga-prepare.yml:72-77 tells the operator to push all three package tags together, which starts three independent workflows rather than a set-level publishing orchestrator.

Verification: .github/workflows/release-coord-engine.yml:240-284, .github/workflows/release-kit.yml:329-353, and .github/workflows/release-drivers.yml:213-237 each push one package to GitHub Packages and then immediately push that same package to nuget.org; no step waits until all three packages are externally verified on GitHub Packages.

Verification: scripts/release-saga.py:227-230 enforces complete-org-first only while recording a later observation, after the package workflows have already crossed the public-feed boundary; no package-owning workflow invokes record-observed before its nuget.org push.

Verification: bash tests/release-saga/run.sh passed on e163d9cdee2a95ca0f3ad951dabbfce5affde146, but tests/release-saga/run.sh:35-69 manually copies and records the complete GitHub set before it records any nuget.org observation, so it does not exercise the production workflow topology that permits interleaving.
resolution_evidence: Verification: repair commit ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660 routes all three package workflows through scripts/release-saga-ci.sh in the ordered init, github-barrier, nuget-probe, NuGet/login, push, and nuget-record sequence; the workflows no longer contain --skip-duplicate.

Verification: scripts/release-saga-ci.sh:56-94 publishes or observes the package-specific org artifact, then downloads and payload-verifies FS.GG.Coord.Cli, FS.GG.Kit, and FS.GG.Drivers together and persists that complete GitHub state before returning success.

Verification: in all three package workflows the GitHub barrier step precedes the public-feed probe and NuGet/login; .github/workflows/release-coord-engine.yml:240-288, .github/workflows/release-kit.yml:329-357, and .github/workflows/release-drivers.yml:213-241 make the public push unreachable until the complete-set barrier returns success.

Verification: tests/release-saga/run.sh's topology check finds the required ordered production tokens in each package workflow and rejects --skip-duplicate; `bash tests/release-saga/run.sh` passed on exact repair head ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660.

findings.summary: The durable retry/recovery journal and resume decisions exercised by the fixture are not wired into production, and preparing the same release again compares a timestamp-mutated manifest byte-for-byte.
evidence: Verification: scripts/release-saga.py:145-164 puts createdAt and updatedAt timestamps in every newly prepared manifest, while .github/workflows/release-saga-prepare.yml:58-65 regenerates that manifest and uses cmp against the prior release asset; even an identical descriptor and package set therefore produces a different manifest on a later run.

Verification: rg -n 'record-failure|record-observed' .github/workflows found record-observed only in .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:63-66 and no production record-failure call; that promotion job runs only when a package workflow concludes success at .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:20-21.

Verification: each package workflow downloads the original draft manifest, asserts only its local package, and then uses dotnet nuget push --skip-duplicate; .github/workflows/release-coord-engine.yml:181-191,240-284, .github/workflows/release-kit.yml:274-284,329-353, and .github/workflows/release-drivers.yml:149-159,213-237 neither read durable per-feed state nor observe an existing remote package before retrying the push.

Verification: tests/release-saga/run.sh:33-54 calls record-observed and record-failure directly on one local manifest before resuming, but no workflow follows that sequence; the green fixture therefore establishes the library's possible state transitions, not production crash recovery or durable resumption.
resolution_evidence: Verification: scripts/release-saga-ci.sh:40-54 resumes the package-specific journal asset when present and otherwise seeds it from the immutable prepared manifest; lines 56-117 observe each target before deciding whether to push, verify the externally served payload afterward, and upload the updated non-racing journal after each monotonic step.

Verification: scripts/release-saga-ci.sh:119-125 records and uploads the current feed/package failure, and each package workflow has an `if: failure()` persistence step immediately after the irreversible feed sequence: engine lines 296-300, Kit lines 365-369, and Drivers lines 249-253.

Verification: .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:39-48 requires exactly three journal assets and merges them before external observation; scripts/release-saga.py:223-271 rejects a different contentId/descriptor or conflicting verified observation while monotonically unioning verified package state and attempts.

Verification: .github/workflows/release-saga-prepare.yml:58-65 now compares an existing release's immutable contentId plus every package byte instead of comparing volatile manifest state bytes, so repeated preparation accepts identical descriptor/artifacts without depending on createdAt or updatedAt.

Verification: `bash tests/release-saga/run.sh`, `bash -n scripts/release-saga-ci.sh tests/release-saga/run.sh`, and `git diff --check e163d9cdee2a95ca0f3ad951dabbfce5affde146..ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660` all exited 0 on exact repair head ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660; shellcheck and actionlint were unavailable.

findings.summary: Publish and promotion do not bind the downloaded manifest's release identity, version, source SHA, and policy to the running workflow, and channel promotion has no cross-release monotonicity guard.
evidence: Verification: scripts/release-saga.py:101-118 assert_bound validates the descriptor contentId and artifact hashes but accepts no expected release ID, version, source SHA, or policy argument; its command-line assert-artifacts surface at lines 306-307 exposes no such expectations.

Verification: the package workflows call that unparameterized assertion after downloading by computed version at .github/workflows/release-coord-engine.yml:188-191, .github/workflows/release-kit.yml:281-284, and .github/workflows/release-drivers.yml:156-159; none checks descriptor.sourceSha against GITHUB_SHA or the descriptor's version/release/policy against the workflow inputs.

Verification: .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:37-41 likewise downloads by the checkout's computed version and only calls assert-artifacts, so the observer does not prove that the draft descriptor names github.event.workflow_run.head_sha before it records and promotes external state.

Verification: scripts/release-saga.py:268-291 prevents a second promotion only inside one manifest, while .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:75-80 unconditionally marks that release latest; it never reads the existing stable-channel receipt or rejects promotion of an older/different release, so re-running a fully served older set can move the repository's latest/stable pointer backward.
resolution_evidence: Verification: repair ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660 resolves the identity half: scripts/release-saga.py:206-224 adds assert-identity for releaseId/version/sourceSha/policyVersion/stable channel, scripts/release-saga-ci.sh:40-54 applies it to both the prepared manifest and resumed journal, and .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:40-43 binds promotion to github.event.workflow_run.head_sha.

Verification: repair ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660 adds previousStableVersion to the content-addressed descriptor, reads the preceding published coherent-set stable-channel receipt in .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:74-84, and scripts/release-saga.py:330-347 rejects a mismatched baseline or non-advancing stable version.

Verification: the channel repair is not yet idempotent under the actual three-trigger topology. After the first observer publishes the draft, a later queued workflow_run sees the just-published current coherent-set release as previous_tag at .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:74-81; scripts/release-saga.py:331-334 then rejects its same contentId before reaching the existing-manifest idempotence arm at lines 348-355.

Verification: tests/release-saga/run.sh:74-81 tests first promotion and a newer-version refusal, but does not rerun promotion with the emitted current stable-channel receipt; its green result therefore does not cover the deterministic second/third observer failure.

Verification: repair-round-2 commit e1c836f9fcc336b896a337d3cb89cf3182af8e7c moves the already-promoted manifest check ahead of prior-channel validation and tests that a second promotion with the emitted same-content receipt reproduces a byte-identical receipt; `bash tests/release-saga/run.sh` passed this new replay on the exact repair head.

Verification: the reordered early return is too broad for an older promoted release. scripts/release-saga.py:330-338 now returns success solely from the manifest's own promoted receipt before reading --previous-channel; if a later stable release exists, replaying this older manifest succeeds and .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:91-94 then unconditionally marks the older release latest, bypassing the cross-release monotonic guard at scripts/release-saga.py:339-355.

Verification: this repository currently has no preceding saga channel receipt: both `git tag -l 'coherent-set/*'` and `gh release list --repo FS-GG/.github --limit 100 --json tagName,isDraft,isLatest --jq '.[] | select(.tagName | startswith("coherent-set/v"))'` produced no output on 2026-08-14. The first 0.54.0 promotion therefore supplies no --previous-channel from .github/workflows/release-saga-promote.yml:74-84.

Verification: on that no-previous-channel path, stable_parts is defined only inside `if args.previous_channel` at scripts/release-saga.py:339-349 but is called unconditionally at line 354; an AST inspection printed `{'stable_parts_definitions': [343], 'stable_parts_calls': [354, 354]}`. Python local function binding is not executed when the branch is false, so the first real saga promotion raises UnboundLocalError rather than promoting 0.54.0.

Verification: tests/release-saga/run.sh always supplies a previous-channel receipt for first promotion and tests a different non-advancing release only with an unpromoted merge-base manifest, so neither the first-ever channel path nor replay of an older already-promoted manifest is covered.

Verification: unverified; repair must support the first saga promotion using descriptor.previousStableVersion when no coherent-set receipt exists, accept exact same-content replay only when the live channel still names that content, reject replay of an older promoted manifest after a newer channel exists, and add both regressions.

findings.summary: M3 has not yet satisfied its exit criterion or the explicit release obligation: the reviewed head records 0.54.0 as source-ahead while the last externally evidenced coherent release remains 0.53.0.
evidence: Verification: docs/reports/2026-08-14-090508-coordination-churn-redesign-roadmap.md leaves M3 unchecked and requires one full coherent-set release to reach both feeds plus a forced mid-publish resume with identical hashes.

Verification: registry/dependencies.yml:900-902 records coord-engine version 0.54.0 but package-version 0.53.0 and explicitly says the source remains ahead until the saga publishes and externally verifies all three packages on both feeds.

Verification: `git tag --points-at e163d9cdee2a95ca0f3ad951dabbfce5affde146`, `git tag -l '*0.54.0*'`, and `git branch -r --contains e163d9cdee2a95ca0f3ad951dabbfce5affde146` produced no output in the supplied worktree; there is no repository evidence at the reviewed head of 0.54.0 release tags, a merged source, or a remotely published coherent set.

Verification: the base-to-head diff changes registry/dependencies.yml package-version only by leaving it at 0.53.0 and adds no completed release manifest, external feed hashes, workflow run IDs, or stable-channel receipt for 0.54.0.
resolution_evidence: Verification: registry/dependencies.yml:900-902 remains truthfully staged at source version 0.54.0 and package-version 0.53.0 on repair head ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660, and the roadmap remains unchecked; no release completion is claimed.

Verification: the non-circular route is a preparatory implementation merge only, not milestone acceptance: .github/workflows/release-saga-prepare.yml is workflow_dispatch and the package workflows consume a draft bound to the exact merged GITHUB_SHA, so the new trusted workflow must first exist on default branch before it can prepare and publish that exact source.

Verification: under the work-roadmap contract this finding remains a major completion gate: after the preparatory workflow repair lands, run the real 0.54.0 prepare/publish/promote sequence, externally verify the persisted hashes and runs, then return a new exact repository head carrying the package-version/roadmap evidence for this same critic's confirmation; do not mark M3 complete or accept the critique before that head.

Verification: repair-round-2 head e1c836f9fcc336b896a337d3cb89cf3182af8e7c changes only the critique artifact, promotion implementation, and its fixture relative to ab1ef446f2fb1a82bfbba2f37dc2db12a9f4d660; registry/dependencies.yml still truthfully records package-version 0.53.0 and the roadmap remains unchecked.
